sources.note: Compares chain-of-thought against answer-only supervision under a protocol where the two conditions differ in nothing but the training target, and finds the rationales buy nothing in-domain for strong backbones while buying 20 to 28 points out of domain -- with a human study attributing the measurable effect to language adherence and inspectability rather than to better reasoning.
sources.title: MathShikkha: A Controlled Study of Answer-Only and Chain-of-Thought Supervision for Bangla Mathematical Reasoning in Small Language Models

sources.note: Builds an industrial-safety reasoning benchmark from two pipelines -- program execution over safety scene graphs, and evidence graphs extracted from real accident-investigation reports -- and shows that general multimodal capability does not transfer to it while a 9B model fine-tuned on its chain-of-thought split matches frontier systems.
sources.title: SafeSceneReason: A Multimodal Reasoning Benchmark Connecting Industrial Hazards with Accident Knowledge

sources.note: Calibrates feature-based data-contamination detectors against the systematic feature shifts that post-training introduces, by measuring how controlled prompt variants move scores on known non-members and then correcting only the recurring shift directions, with the gains concentrated at the low-false-positive operating point rather than in AUC.
sources.title: Calibrating Post-Training Feature Shifts for LLM Data Contamination Detection

sources.note: Injects a retrieved solved problem, with its full worked solution, into the middle of a reasoning model's own thinking trace at each step boundary, using the model's current intermediate answer as the retrieval query.
sources.title: ThinkRetrieve: Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning Traces for Test-Time Scaling

instructions:
Write the wiki definition for 'decontamination'.

The sources below are every archived paper and talk that mentions it. Define it as they use it: if they disagree, say so; if the term is used loosely, say that too.

`related` is the one part of the note nothing can work out on its own. The wiki already links entities that turn up in the same summary; what it cannot see is the neighbour a reader would actually want next — the generation before this one, the benchmark it was built to beat, the method it replaces. Name those. Leave the list empty rather than repeating what the sources already put side by side.

Rules:
- Write in en.
- Ground every statement in the supplied material. If something is not stated,
  leave the field empty rather than inferring it.
- No marketing language. Prefer the specific number over the adjective.
- Return one JSON object matching the schema exactly. No prose around it.

aliases: string - other names the sources use for the same thing
output_schema.definition: string - two to four sentences defining the entity as the cited sources use it, not as a textbook would
output_schema.kind: string - one of: concept, method, dataset, model
related: string - name of a neighbouring entity worth linking to. Kept as you give it and never derived away, so name what a reader should turn to next rather than what happens to appear alongside this. Answering again replaces the whole list; an empty list retracts

result.definition: Removing training items that overlap evaluation items, and across 4 sources a procedure the archive reads as a threshold choice with consequences rather than a hygiene step. The instances that report their own numbers are the useful ones. One audit runs three stages, flags one problem in an external benchmark, confirms it by inspection as a false positive, and reports maximum problem-level similarity to any training item at 0.84 with a median of 0.53 -- which is what makes its 20-to-28-point rationale-supervision result readable. Another decontaminates by cosine similarity at 0.90 and reports maximum retained similarities of 0.898 and 0.891, immediately below the cut, with means of 0.866 and 0.845; it attributes this to the structural density of synthetic mathematics corpora rather than to leakage and defends the choice with an answer-distinct retrieval control rather than by lowering the threshold. A third removes flagged overlaps at three levels -- problem, solution and skill card -- and retrains every reported model afterwards. The archive's reading is that decontamination establishes implausibility rather than absence, that the retained-similarity distribution is the number to report, and that a control distinguishing structural similarity from leakage is what makes a threshold defensible.
